name: dusty packed wasteland earth ground, a seamless 4x4-tile field with soft tonal patches, long dry cracks and pebbles running across tile borders, mixed with tiles of dry grass tufts
label: wasteland_ruins/dirt-d

surfaces.part: ground field (packed earth, cracks, pebbles, grass tufts)

answer.evidence: The image is a seamless flat 96x80 terrain field with a uniform full-width silhouette (rows 0-79 at width 96). It has tonal patches, cracks and pebbles seen from above, with no front face, no eave line, no ellipse and no side face. The column scans show only texture variation, not a top surface and front face structure. As terrain tiles, it is a flat top-down surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 12 colours in total. The grey-mauve base is a large, mostly flat field, with sparse brown patches, thin dark cracks and a few light pebbles on top. Near-flat coverage is 33%, while both references are at 0%, so a third of the ground is unbroken fill with no grain or speckle. The visible tones per tile (7) match the paving reference and beat the grass (3), but they sit in the patch and crack tiles. The plain base areas look thinner than the references' constant dotting and clumping. The brown patches have about 3 tones (base, mid brown, dark brown) and no highlight/shadow ramp, against roughly 5-6 steps in Beodeul materials. The cracks and patch edges are tinted dark brown (0% neutral dark edge pixels), so there is no sticker-style black outline. The yellow dots look like stray accents rather than shaded stones. The patches read as soft and tonal, but the texture is too sparse and the flat base too extensive for Beodeul quality.

Beodeul grounds have 5-6 steps and grain across the whole surface, so this is shallower and flatter than the references.

Darker and lighter patches, thin crack lines, and pebbles are texture across a flat ground plane. This is correct for terrain tiles and is a flat top-down surface with no standing front face.

As terrain it is a flat top-down surface with no front face, so it reads as top_down_slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured tones per tile are 7, against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving, so the tone count alone is not the problem. The weak points are structural. Next to the references this looks flatter and thinner than the grass tile, which has no flat area at all.
